props.title: Leaving Las Vegas
props.initialSlug: When love is all you have left.
props.initialStreaming: fuboTV, MGM+ Amazon Channel, MGM Plus

sections.content: Leaving Las Vegas (1995) stands as one of cinema's most unflinching portraits of addiction and self-destruction. Nicolas Cage delivers a career-defining, Oscar-winning performance as Ben Sanderson, a suicidal alcoholic who heads to Vegas to drink himself to death. His raw, devastating portrayal alongside Elisabeth Shue's nuanced take on Sera, a sex worker who forms an unusual bond with Ben, creates a love story unlike anything in mainstream American cinema. Director Mike Figgis shot on 16mm film with a minimal crew, giving the film a gritty documentary feel that amplifies its emotional authenticity.

movies.title: The Lost Weekend
movies.slug: Ray Milland's Oscar-winning role as a writer on a four-day drinking binge set the template for addiction dramas

sections.content: The film's unflinching approach to addiction influenced later works like Requiem for a Dream (2000) and Clean and Sober (1988). While most Hollywood films about addiction focus on recovery or redemption, Leaving Las Vegas boldly commits to showing the terminal stage of alcoholism without moral judgment or false hope. This approach shares DNA with European art films like Oslo, August 31st (2011) and The Fire Within (1963), which similarly tackle suicide and addiction with stark realism.

The Las Vegas setting provides a perfect backdrop for Ben's descent - a neon-lit purgatory where time loses meaning. Unlike glossy Vegas films like Casino (1995) or Ocean's Eleven (2001), Figgis captures the city's grimy underbelly, shooting in actual dive bars and cheap motels. This documentary-style approach influenced later indie films like Factotum (2005) and The Wrestler (2008) in their portrayal of characters living on society's margins. SUBHEAD: Breaking Hollywood Conventions

movies.title: Days of Wine and Roses
movies.slug: Jack Lemmon and Lee Remick shine as a married couple whose lives are torn apart by alcoholism

sections.content: The film's structure deliberately subverts traditional addiction narrative arcs. There's no intervention scene, no recovery attempt, no moment of clarity - just an honest portrait of a man at peace with his fatal decision. This influenced later works like Flight (2012) and Half Nelson (2006) in their complex portrayal of functional addicts. The unusual love story between Ben and Sera also breaks convention - their agreement to accept each other without trying to change one another stands in stark contrast to typical Hollywood redemption narratives.
